title: Activepieces vs Workato: Features & Pricing (2026)
summary: Activepieces vs Workato: one is open-source and self-hosted with published pricing; the other is a sales-led enterprise platform.
body_markdown:
## Integrations and embedding in your own product


If you depend on an enterprise system Workato covers, it wins, because it lists more pre-built connectors.


For embedding automation inside your own SaaS product, the open-source tool offers a white-label flow builder, AI agents and 744 integrations inside your own product, which means coverage for nearly any integration need, from $36,000 a year through sales.


Workato publishes **1,200+ pre-built connectors against 744 integrations** in the open-source monorepo, meaning substantially greater integration coverage than the open-source tool provides. That gap matters only if your stack sits in the difference.


If your must-have is a large ERP or HR system that Workato covers and the other tool doesn't, the count settles it, and no amount of flexibility elsewhere makes up for it.


If both cover your core systems, the question changes: what happens when a connector is missing? Workato offers a connector SDK, so you build the missing integration yourself.


You can read how any existing integration in the open-source tool works, fork it, or write a new one, because they are TypeScript packages in a public repository.


In both cases a custom connector is code your team owns and maintains when the vendor's API changes. Count how many of those you expect to write before you trust either headline number.


### Embedding automation in your product


When you embed automation, your customers build or run automations inside your app, under your brand, without knowing a separate tool exists. That's a different purchase from running internal workflows.


You need to control how it looks, how customer accounts are separated, and what it costs per customer, because that cost lands in your own margins.


Built around an IT team automating the company's own systems, Workato prices its embedded offering by quote. That works if you have enterprise budget and a sales cycle.


A bootstrapped SaaS team will usually care more about a cost model it can predict before signing anything.


The open-source tool is designed so a product team can put its builder and flows inside another application, and its open-source core means you can inspect what you're embedding.


Because embedding terms depend on your scale and whether you self-host, they go through the sales form at[https://www.activepieces.com/sales](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) rather than a self-serve plan.
